Figures and tables for the report, built with the `retractionwatch` package.

How countries are counted:

* **Each country:** a paper counts once in every country of its authors.
* **Groups:** a paper counts once, in a single group:
  * **United Kingdom:** at least one UK author.
  * **Other OECD:** no UK author, but at least one author from another OECD country.
  * **Rest of World:** no author from the UK or another OECD country.
* **Papers with no known country** ("Unknown" in Retraction Watch) are left out.

Retraction Watch entries include all notice types (retractions, expressions of concern, corrections and reinstatements). Mass retractions (IEEE 2009–2011, Hindawi 2022–2024) are included.

```{r setup, include=FALSE, message=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r}
devtools::load_all("retractionwatch", quiet = TRUE)
library(plotly)

sjr_country_counts <- build_sjr_country_counts("data/sjr_rankings")
oecd_countries <- load_oecd_countries("data/oecd_countries.csv")
retraction_data <- load_retraction_data("data/retraction_watch.csv", oecd_countries)
```

# AI retractions in the 10 OECD countries with most retractions

The 10 OECD countries with the most retractions, excluding mass retractions, as on the [library analysis page](retraction-analysis-library.qmd). Counts and rates cover papers published in 2017–2025, when almost all AI retractions happen, for both the retractions and the SCImago publication counts. A retraction mentions AI when one of its reasons is "Computer-Aided Content" or "Computer-Generated Content". Intervals are exact 95% confidence intervals (binomial for percentages, Poisson for rates).

```{r}
ai_years <- c(2017, 2025)

# A paper with authors in several countries counts once for each of them
top_10_oecd_countries <- retraction_data |>
  filter(Mass_Retraction == "Other", Country %in% oecd_countries$Name) |>
  distinct(`Record ID`, Country) |>
  count(Country, name = "retractions", sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)

retraction_ai_rates <- compute_ai_rates_by_country(retraction_data, sjr_country_counts,
                                                   publication_years = ai_years)

knitr::kable(ai_rates_table(retraction_ai_rates, top_10_oecd_countries, "All"),
             format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
             caption = "AI retractions of papers published 2017–2025, all retractions, sorted by rate per 100,000 papers")
```

# AI retractions as a proportion of all retractions

For each publication year, the proportion of retractions in each group that mention AI. Shaded bands are exact 95% binomial confidence intervals. The y axis is pseudo-log: linear near 0 and logarithmic above, so years with no AI retractions still show at 0.

```{r}
retraction_ai_prop_ts <- compute_ai_proportion_ts(retraction_data) |>
  filter(scenario == "All")

autorange_axes(ggplotly(
  plot_ai_ts(retraction_ai_prop_ts, "prop_ai",
             "Retractions mentioning AI (pseudo-log scale, 95% CI)",
             labels = scales::label_percent(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
    theme(strip.text = element_blank())
))
```

# Top 10 retraction reasons in the UK and the rest of the OECD

The 10 reasons cited by the most Other OECD retractions from 2017 onwards, as a single list. Each panel shows the yearly proportion of that group's retractions citing each reason, by retraction year. A retraction can cite several reasons, so the proportions in a year can add up to more than 100%. Years with fewer than 20 retractions (UK) or 80 (Other OECD) are left out, as on the library page.

```{r}
retraction_data_uk <- subset(retraction_data, country_class == "United Kingdom")
retraction_data_oecd <- subset(retraction_data, country_class == "Other OECD")

top_10_reasons <- top_reasons_overall(retraction_data_oecd, n = 10,
                                      year_limits = c(2017, 2025))

knitr::kable(tibble::tibble(Rank = seq_along(top_10_reasons), Reason = top_10_reasons),
             caption = "Top 10 reasons in Other OECD retractions since 2017")
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 9
ggplotly(
  plot_reasons_over_time_by_group(
    list("United Kingdom" = retraction_data_uk, "Other OECD" = retraction_data_oecd),
    reasons_list = top_10_reasons,
    min_retractions_per_year = c(20, 80),
    year_limits = c(2000, 2025)),
  height = 900)
```
